papers.title_en: Better Nearest Neighbor Graph Indices via (Efficient) LLM-Guided Pruning
papers.authors: Fangzhou Wu, Haike Xu, Sandeep Silwal
papers.evidence: 基于图的近似最近邻搜索索引构建
papers.tldr: 基于图的近似最近邻搜索广泛用于大规模语义检索，但图索引主要按嵌入的几何关系构建，而检索效果却按结果与查询的语义相关性评估，形成根本性的几何-语义错配。现有LLM重排只能在查询阶段部分缓解，无法解决图结构本身的问题。为此，论文提出LLM引导图剪枝LGP：识别节点中结构上低价值的邻居，并用LLM选择的替代邻居替换，在引入有用语义信息的同时保持原图的稀疏性与可导航性。在代表性语义检索基准上，LGP对DiskANN、HNSW等主流图索引均持续提升端到端检索性能，并优于原始贪心图搜索和LLM重排。
papers.abstract_en: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) is widely used for large-scale semantic search. Its indices are constructed primarily based on geometric relationships among embeddings of an input dataset (e.g., documents or images), rather than explicitly optimizing for semantic relevance. However, when using these indices for downstream query retrieval, performance is evaluated based on the semantic relevance of the retrieved results to the query. This creates a fundamental "geometry-semantic" mismatch between how the indices are constructed and how their retrieval results are evaluated. While existing LLM-based reranking methods can partially mitigate this mismatch at query time, they leave this underlying structural problem in the graph unresolved. We therefore propose LLM-Guided Graph Pruning (LGP), a general framework that addresses this mismatch directly by leveraging LLM reasoning to refine an existing ANN graph index itself. LGP identifies structurally "low-value" neighbors of nodes and replaces them with LLM-selected alternatives that provide useful semantic information while retaining desired geometric structures of the original graph, including sparsity and efficient navigability. Experiments on representative semantic retrieval benchmarks show that LGP consistently improves end-to-end retrieval performance over both vanilla greedy graph search and LLM-based reranking across widely used graph-based ANN indices such as DiskANN and HNSW.
